_note: Pilot bios for the Mech Bay's personnel screen (issue I86 follow-up). Written for the remake: the original's FlavorText was never set. Drafts for Lee's review; keyed by profile.
pmwchopper: Chopper came up through a salvage crew, cutting wrecks apart for scrap before anyone let him climb into a working cockpit. He shoots straighter than he walks a 'Mech, and he still sizes up every wreck on the field for its parts.
pmwcobra: Cobra is patient at the controls and steadier on her feet than most green pilots, though her gunnery still needs work. She says little on the comms and waits for her opening before she strikes.
pmwcreep: Creep earned the name in training by sneaking a 'Mech up on his instructors through broken ground. His footwork is good for a recruit; his aim and his sensor work are still catching up.
pmwdagger: Dagger is a close-quarters fighter who likes to close the range and settle things fast. She is an average pilot with a better-than-average trigger finger, and she wants a heavier 'Mech than she has earned.
pmwflash: Flash is quick on the sticks and quicker with an answer. He is one of the better green pilots for keeping a 'Mech upright on rough ground. His gunnery lags behind his footwork, and he knows it.
pmwhacksaw: Hacksaw spent years as a 'Mech technician before switching to the cockpit, and she still fixes her own machine between drops. She has no standout skill but no real weakness, and she is steady under fire.
pmwhammer: Hammer's answer to most problems is to hit them again, harder. He is among the better shots in the new intake but one of its weakest pilots, so keep him out of terrain that punishes clumsy footwork.
pmwjinx: Jinx has walked away from more bad landings than anyone in the company, which is how she got the name. She is the most sure-footed of the recruits; her gunnery is the part still in training.
pmwlongshot: Longshot is a born spotter, with sharp eyes on the sensors and a patient trigger at range. On the ground he is the least steady pilot in the intake, so he does best standing back and letting the targets come to him.
pmwmeat: Meat signed on as a hired gun who knows his way around a medium autocannon. Behind the blunt manners he has a good eye on the sensors, and he is better at reading a fight than he lets on.
pmwpalerider: Palerider is quiet and hard to read. She has a knack for keeping her 'Mech off enemy sensors that the training cadre never taught her. She is a fair shot and a fair pilot who would rather not be seen until she fires.
pmwpsycho: Psycho volunteers for the jobs nobody else wants and enjoys them a little too much. He is a good shot and a poor pilot, and he is better kept on a short leash in a lance than left to roam alone.
pmwshadow: Shadow is a dependable all-rounder who does what is asked of her and seldom more. She rarely complains, rarely shines and rarely misses a drop, and plenty of commanders would settle for that.
pmwtwitch: Twitch has nervous hands and a laser specialist's eye, a mix that works better than it sounds. He picks up targets fast on the sensors and gets his shots off before most pilots have finished aiming.
pmwworm: Worm is a sensor operator who earned her way into a cockpit. She is good at keeping her 'Mech off enemy scopes and better at finding theirs. She treats a fight as a search problem first.
pmwsteel: Steel is a hard-bitten veteran of the merc circuit with more scars than medals, and he can take a beating and keep walking. His sensor work is the best of the early hires, and he will tell you so.
pmwbubba: Bubba is a medium-'Mech specialist who knows the autocannon inside and out. He has a slow drawl and a quick trigger. Mid-weight companies have been glad to have him for years, and this one is no different.
pmwscooter: Scooter can put a jumping 'Mech exactly where she wants it and reads the sensors better than anyone short of the company's best. She is less of a shot than a scout, and the lance's eyes on every drop she makes.
pmwvenom: Venom is a scout who likes to finish what she finds, preferably with an extended-range laser. She has a sharp eye and a sharper tongue, and she would rather hunt alone than wait for the lance.
pmwwicked: Wicked is a fire-support pilot who carries lasers for anything close and missiles for everything else. She is one of the best shots on this contract, and she knows exactly what she is worth.
pmwclaymore: Claymore is built like his 'Mech and fights like it: he plants himself in the line and takes the hits so others don't have to. His gunnery and piloting are middling, but his toughness is not.
pmwpayback: Payback holds grudges and settles them with a light autocannon. She is a solid shot with an average hand on the controls, and she came to this contract with something to prove to somebody.
pmwnuke: Nuke loves short-range missiles and the noise they make, and his sensor work is better than his manners. He is a poor pilot in rough terrain, so give him a clear line to the target and stand back.
pmwghost: Ghost is a veteran scout who makes long jumps, takes long shots and leaves almost no sensor trace. Among the hired guns he is the best pilot in the cockpit, and he seldom stays where the enemy last saw him.
pmwmother: Mother has the best sensors and some of the sharpest gunnery in the company, and she treats every lance as hers to bring home. She specialises in medium 'Mechs, lasers and heavy autocannons, and she will not lose a pilot if she can help it.
pmwrooster: Rooster is loud and proud, and good enough that it hardly matters. He is a heavy-hitting veteran with long-range missiles and a PPC, and he can take punishment better than most and dish it out better still.
